gaps.note: The page does not say which map of the network is its endpoint operator, or how the network realises the shear. The linked shear page does not define the phrase, so the reader cannot tell what is being identified with the shear.

gaps.quote: The geometric sum is also $O(m^{k\tau})$, since it is $O((s/W)^k)$.
gaps.note: A geometric sum with ratio r is O(r^k) only when r>1. The page gives only s/W<m and never a lower bound on s/W. For r<1 the sum is bounded, not O(r^k), so the stated reason does not hold in general.
Nothing on the page states or gives m>=2, so the reason offered for both bounds cannot be checked from the page.

Unrolling Q_k <= (s/W) Q_{k-1} + C gives plus C times the sum, not minus. The stated minus sign cannot be derived from the recurrence, and as written the bound is false in general (for k=1 it gives Q_1 <= (s/W) Q_0 - C).

The page introduces Q_0=O(1) with 'Hence', but the level-k description it follows from only covers k>=1. Nothing on the page describes the level-0 interchange of one-bit fields, so the constant bound is unsupported.
